section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the gathering of the harvest corresponds to gathering all aspects of Torah—its four levels of interpretation—and unifying them, which is a foretaste of the future redemption, yet is also accessible now.
section.t: And this is “and the Festival of the Harvest… when you gather in your labors from the field,”
which is the gathering of all matters together.
And the beginning of this is that one gathers all the matters of Torah
(like all the divine services,
whose beginning is in their essence as it is in Torah,
since “He looked into the Torah and created the world”).
For behold, every matter in Torah has six hundred thousand explanations according to the plain meaning,
six hundred thousand explanations according to the allegorical meaning,
and likewise according to the homiletical meaning and according to the secret meaning.
And one must gather and include all the explanations of the part of the plain meaning,
and likewise all the explanations of the part of the allegorical meaning,
of the part of the homiletical meaning and of the part of the secret meaning,
and after this to gather and include all four parts together.
And this is “and you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil,”
grain
(bread)
is the revealed aspect of Torah,
wine
(wine)
is the secrets of Torah,
and oil
(oil)
is the secrets of secrets,
and the service of “and you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil” is twofold.
The gathering and inclusion of the multitude of matters of each category
(revealed,
secrets, and secrets of secrets)
itself,
and also the gathering and inclusion of all the categories together,
and to elevate them to a level above division,
until the aspect of “the place that includes everything”
and higher.
And although the main point of this matter
(the unification of all matters of Torah)
will be at the coming of Moshiach,
who will teach the entire people
the entire Torah,
also the secrets of Torah and the secrets of secrets,
and as it is written,
“Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth,” and Rashi explains that in the future the secret of its reasons
(of Torah)
and the hidden mysteries will be revealed,
and all this will be then in a manner of sight,
nevertheless,
since “those who taste it merit life,”
behold, a foretaste of this in a manner of tasting at least can be and must be now.
And from this
(from the matter of “and you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil” as it is in Torah)
it is drawn down that there should be “and you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil” in all matters of man’s service in spirituality,
and even that this is drawn down also in “and you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil” literally,
in physical grain, wine, and oil.
And likewise is it also regarding the matter of the unity of dwelling in the sukkah
(after the service of gathering),
that in this there are
(as above)
two levels,
“In sukkot you shall dwell for seven days,” which is the matter of unity as it still pertains to seven days
(division)
and “all the native-born in Israel shall dwell in sukkot”
(simply,
above the matter of seven days),
that the main point of this matter will be in the future,
as is known
that the explanation of “native-born” (ezrach) is that which is destined to shine (lehazriach) in the future,
except that nevertheless there is an illumination of this also now.
As the explanation of the Baal HaHilula
(based on this),
that that which is destined to shine in the future within Israel and in their innerness,
behold also now “they shall dwell in sukkot,”
that this is revealed upon them
(now)
in the aspect of sukkah and encompassing light.
And likewise is it also regarding the matter of the four species
(for the taking of the four species is
(as above)
after the dwelling in the sukkah),
that each of the four species is “this is the Holy One, blessed be He,”
that this matter is also now,
except that now it is in concealment,
and the revelation of this will be in the future, when “the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see,” etc.
And then there will also be “the gathering of your grain, your wine, and your oil” in a different manner,
that it will not need to be “and you shall gather”
(that Israel will need to gather)
but rather “and strangers shall stand and shepherd your flocks, and foreigners shall be your plowmen,” etc.,
and also the dwelling in the sukkah will be in a more elevated manner,
“they shall dwell in the sukkah of the skin of the Leviathan,”
and also this matter of “this is the Holy One, blessed be He”
(that is in the four species)
will then be revealed,
as “as I am written, so I am read,”
except that a foretaste of this
(of all these matters)
exists also now,
and as above in the explanation of “all the native-born in Israel shall dwell in sukkot,”
and all the more so in the time of the end of the exile
(the footsteps of Moshiach)
that only a few moments remain,
and the Torah promised that Israel will ultimately repent at the end of their exile and immediately they are redeemed,
with joy and a good heart.
